    //==
    // # The subdivision scheme driver
    //
    // `SubdivisionScheme` and `SubdivisionSurface` (`surfaces.types.plato`) named a
    // scheme and a refinement level with nothing behind either. These are the
    // bodies: one level of the named scheme, and the level count driving repeated
    // application.
    //
    // Loop is a TRIANGLE scheme, so on a polygon mesh it triangulates first; the
    // result is a triangle mesh re-expressed as a polygon mesh, which is what makes
    // the three schemes composable through one signature.

    // A triangle mesh expressed as a polygon mesh: every face is a three-row.
    ToPolygonMesh(self: TriangleMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(self.Positions, self.Faces.Map(f => f.Vertices));

    // One level of the named scheme.
    SubdividedOnce(self: PolygonMesh3D, scheme: SubdivisionScheme): PolygonMesh3D
        => match (scheme) {
            CatmullClark => self.CatmullClarkSubdivided;
            Loop => self.ToTriangleMesh.LoopSubdivided.ToPolygonMesh;
            DooSabin => self.DooSabinSubdivided;
        };

    // The named scheme applied `levels` times. Each level multiplies the face
    // count by roughly four, and the cost of a level is quadratic in the corner
    // count, so the cost of the last level dominates everything before it.
    Subdivided(self: PolygonMesh3D, scheme: SubdivisionScheme, levels: Integer): PolygonMesh3D
        => Repeat(levels, 0).Reduce(self, (mesh, level) => mesh.SubdividedOnce(scheme));

    // The refined control mesh of a subdivision surface: its own scheme applied
    // its own number of times. This is the approximation `SubdivisionSurface`
    // (`surfaces.types.plato`) describes; the true limit surface is not evaluated.
    RefinedControlMesh(self: SubdivisionSurface): PolygonMesh3D
        => self.ControlMesh.Subdivided(self.Scheme, self.Levels);

    //==
    // # Smoothing
    //
    // Moving vertices without changing connectivity. Every step computes one
    // displacement per vertex against the CURRENT positions and applies them all
    // at once, which is the Jacobi form — a Gauss-Seidel sweep would make the
    // result depend on vertex order, and there is no order in an expression.
    //
    // Boundary vertices are pinned throughout. A Laplacian step moves a boundary
    // vertex inward, so smoothing an open mesh without pinning shrinks its border
    // visibly in a handful of iterations.

    // The uniform Laplacian at a vertex: the offset from it to the average of its
    // neighbours (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplacian_smoothing).
    UniformLaplacian(positions: Array<Point3D>, neighbors: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>, v: Integer): Vector3D
        => neighbors[v].Count.IsZero
            ? Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
            : positions[v].Between(neighbors[v].Map(n => positions[n.Value]).AverageOfPoints);

    // The cotangent of the angle at `apex` in the triangle apex-a-b, as the ratio
    // of the dot product to the cross-product magnitude of the two side vectors.
    // A degenerate triangle contributes nothing rather than an infinity.
    CotangentAtApex(apex: Point3D, a: Point3D, b: Point3D): Number
    {
        var u = apex.Between(a);
        var w = apex.Between(b);
        var area = u.Cross(w).Magnitude;
        return area <= 0.0 ? 0.0 : u.Dot(w) / area;
    }

    // The cotangent weight of one undirected edge: cot(alpha) + cot(beta) over the
    // angles facing it in its two triangles, or the single cotangent on a boundary
    // edge (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_Laplace_operator).
    EdgeCotangentWeight(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer): Number
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var a = self.Positions[pair.A.Value];
        var b = self.Positions[pair.B.Value];
        var near = self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var far = self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        return CotangentAtApex(self.Positions[near.Value], a, b)
            + (far.IsNone ? 0.0 : CotangentAtApex(self.Positions[far.Value], a, b));
    }

    // The cotangent weight of every undirected edge, in edge order.
    EdgeCotangentWeights(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology): Array<Number>
        => topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => self.EdgeCotangentWeight(topology, e));

    // The cotangent Laplacian at a vertex: the weighted average offset to its
    // neighbours. Obtuse triangles give negative weights, so the normalizing sum
    // can vanish; that vertex then does not move.
    CotangentLaplacian(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, weights: Array<Number>, v: Integer): Vector3D
    {
        var edges = topology.UndirectedEdges;
        var total = topology.EdgeCount
            .MapRange(e => PairTouches(edges[e], v) ? weights[e] : 0.0)
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, w) => acc + w);
        var sum = topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => e).Reduce(Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), (acc, e) =>
            PairTouches(edges[e], v)
                ? acc + self.Positions[v].Between(self.Positions[PairOtherEnd(edges[e], v).Value]) * weights[e]
                : acc);
        return total.Abs <= 0.0 ? Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) : sum * (1.0 / total);
    }

    // The uniform Laplacian of every vertex.
    UniformLaplacianField(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology): Array<Vector3D>
    {
        var neighbors = self.VertexNeighborTable(topology);
        return self.Positions.Count.MapRange(v => UniformLaplacian(self.Positions, neighbors, v));
    }

    // The cotangent Laplacian of every vertex.
    CotangentLaplacianField(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology): Array<Vector3D>
    {
        var weights = self.EdgeCotangentWeights(topology);
        return self.Positions.Count.MapRange(v => self.CotangentLaplacian(topology, weights, v));
    }

    // The displacement one smoothing step gives each vertex under the chosen
    // weighting, before the step size is applied.
    LaplacianField(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, weighting: LaplacianWeighting): Array<Vector3D>
        => match (weighting) {
            UniformWeights => self.UniformLaplacianField(topology);
            CotangentWeights => self.CotangentLaplacianField(topology);
        };

    // One Laplacian step: every interior vertex moves `strength` of the way along
    // its Laplacian. A negative strength is the inflating half of Taubin's pair.
    LaplacianStep(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, weighting: LaplacianWeighting, strength: Number): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var field = self.LaplacianField(topology, weighting);
        var boundary = self.BoundaryVertexFlags(topology);
        return (self.Positions.Count.MapRange(v =>
                    boundary[v] ? self.Positions[v] : self.Positions[v] + field[v] * strength),
                self.Faces);
    }

    // Laplacian smoothing, repeated. Every step shrinks the surface a little; use
    // `TaubinSmoothed` where that matters.
    //
    // The connectivity is built ONCE and reused by every iteration, which is sound
    // precisely because smoothing moves vertices and never touches the face table.
    // That is the design decision paying off: because the topology is a derived,
    // read-only value rather than a structure being edited, an invariant pass can
    // simply keep it.
    LaplacianSmoothed(self: TriangleMesh3D, weighting: LaplacianWeighting, strength: Number, iterations: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return Repeat(iterations, 0).Reduce(self, (mesh, step) =>
            mesh.LaplacianStep(topology, weighting, strength));
    }

    // One Taubin iteration: a shrinking step of `lambda` and an inflating step of
    // `mu` over the same connectivity.
    TaubinStep(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, weighting: LaplacianWeighting,
               lambda: Number, mu: Number): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.LaplacianStep(topology, weighting, lambda)
            .LaplacianStep(topology, weighting, mu);
